title: The Parking Validation
synopsis: Jerry becomes obsessed with a parking garage that won't validate his ticket unless he spends at least ten dollars at an attached gift shop, leading him into an escalating war of principle with the garage attendant. George, convinced his new girlfriend's family thinks he's "too agreeable," starts manufacturing fake opinions and hobbies to seem more interesting, which spirals when he claims to be a collector of antique globes. Elaine discovers that her new assistant has been secretly rewriting her emails to sound "nicer," making her seem suspiciously warm to coworkers who now think something's wrong with her. Kramer gets into the business of "validating" people's problems as a form of emotional therapy he calls "Vali-Date," charging friends and strangers five dollars to simply agree with them about anything. The threads collide when Jerry, desperate to avoid the ten-dollar gift shop purchase, buys a cheap antique-looking globe as a gag gift for George to keep up his lie, only to discover it's the same globe Kramer sold to a client that morning as part of a "Vali-Date" session gone wrong, all while Elaine's assistant "validates" Jerry's parking rage in an email that gets forwarded to the entire building.
scene:
INT. MONK'S CAFE - BOOTH - DAY

(JERRY and GEORGE sit across from each other. JERRY looks irritated, stirring his coffee aggressively.)

JERRY: Ten dollars. TEN DOLLARS. I was in that garage for eleven minutes.

GEORGE: So buy a candy bar.

JERRY: I don't want a candy bar! I want validation for existing in a parking garage for eleven minutes!

GEORGE: Welcome to a committed relationship.

(JERRY looks up, unimpressed.)

JERRY: What's going on with you? You've got a weird energy today.

GEORGE: (defensive) I collect globes.

JERRY: Since when?

GEORGE: Since Donna's family thinks I have no interests. So now I have interests. I have a globe interest.

JERRY: You don't even have a bookshelf.

GEORGE: I'll get a bookshelf! For the globes!

(KRAMER bursts in, clipboard in hand, wearing a lanyard that says "VALI-DATE.")

KRAMER: Gentlemen. Either of you need validating today?

JERRY: Kramer, what is that.

KRAMER: It's a service. People just want to be heard, Jerry. Five bucks, I agree with whatever you're feeling. No judgment.

GEORGE: I'm feeling like I need a globe.

KRAMER: (writing on clipboard, nodding solemnly) That's valid. That is a valid feeling.

JERRY: He's not actually into globes, Kramer, he's lying to his girlfriend's family.

KRAMER: (still nodding) Also valid.

JERRY: Everything's valid to you!

KRAMER: That's the business, Jerry!

(ELAINE enters, phone in hand, scrolling furiously.)

ELAINE: You will not believe what my assistant did. She rewrote my email to IT and now everyone thinks I'm "deeply sorry for the inconvenience and grateful for their patience."

JERRY: Were you?

ELAINE: I called them morons in all caps!

KRAMER: (pulling out a five from Elaine's purse before she notices) That's valid too.

ELAINE: Kramer!

KRAMER: (writing on clipboard) She's upset. Noted.

(JERRY stands, pulling out his car keys, done with all of them.)

JERRY: I have to go fight a parking garage.

GEORGE: Get me a globe while you're out.

JERRY: I'm not getting you a globe.

(He exits. KRAMER turns to GEORGE, clipboard ready.)

KRAMER: You feel dismissed.

GEORGE: I feel dismissed!

KRAMER: Valid.

(ELAINE drops her head onto the table, groaning, as KRAMER writes on his clipboard without looking up.)

KRAMER: Also valid.

CUT TO BLACK.
